sections.body:
## Why no scaffolding

Scaffolding a tall structure can take days to erect and strike, takes up space, and adds exposure for other workers. For local repairs, painting, or light installation, a rope access team rigs within hours and starts work. We break the costs down in our article on [rope access versus scaffolding](/en/rope-access-vs-scaffolding-inspection-cost/).

## When scaffolding is still the right choice

We will tell you honestly: work that needs a wide platform for heavy materials, or very long stays at one point, usually suits scaffolding better. Our initial survey decides the most efficient method.

## Working in live operations

In factories, warehouses, or buildings that keep operating, work is arranged with the site manager: permits to work, energy isolation where needed, and protection of the area below the work zone.

## Need renovation or construction?

For work bigger than repairs at height — renovation, construction, or design — our group company [Inland](https://inland.co.id/en/services/) handles [contractor services](https://inland.co.id/en/contractor-services/) and [building maintenance](https://inland.co.id/en/building-maintenance-services/), while RAC delivers the parts that need rope access.

columns.title: Scope of work
items: Painting towers, tanks, chimneys, and steel structures
Repairing roofs, gutters, and wall cladding

Sealant and waterproofing on high walls
Cleaning structures and ducts at height

sections.title: Four steps from survey to report

items.title: 1. Survey & quotation
items.text: We review the site or your photos and drawings, then send the scope, method, schedule, and a written quotation.

items.title: 2. Work plan & permits
items.text: A risk assessment, method statement, and rescue plan are prepared before work starts; permits are arranged with the site manager.

items.title: 3. Delivery
items.text: A team of Kemnaker-certified technicians works with a supervisor on site; the area below the work zone is secured.

items.title: 4. Report & handover
items.text: Before-and-after photos and a work report are handed over with recommendations for the next maintenance cycle.

items.a: Local work spread over many points — repainting, repairs, light installation, cleaning — is usually most efficient by rope access. Heavy materials or very long stays at one point can suit scaffolding better.

items.q: Does the plant have to stop?
items.a: Usually not. Work is scheduled with the site manager, with the work area protected and energy isolated only where necessary.
Either works: materials from the owner, or we procure them to an agreed specification. It is all set out in the quotation.

sections.title: Tell us about the job
sections.text: Send the location, the type of building or asset, and your target dates. We reply with a written quotation, usually the same working day.
